snapshot.text: Infosys is a global IT services company whose consolidated FY2026 (year ended March 31, 2026) revenue was ₹1,78,650 crore (US$20,158 million), crossing the $20 billion mark with 9.6% reported growth and 3.1% constant-currency growth.

The company operates across business segments including Financial Services, Manufacturing, Energy/Utilities/Resources/Services, Retail, Communication, Hi-Tech and Life Sciences, with Financial Services the largest segment at ₹49,908 crore of FY2026 consolidated revenue.
Infosys has no outstanding borrowings and held consolidated cash and investments of ₹43,075 crore as of FY2026, with growth financed largely through operating cash flows.

financials.text: FY2026 consolidated revenue was ₹1,78,650 crore, up 9.6% reported and 3.1% in constant currency versus FY2025 revenue of ₹1,62,990 crore.
FY2026 consolidated net profit attributable to owners was ₹29,440 crore (US$3,313 million), up 10.2% YoY, with basic EPS of ₹71.58 (up 11.0%).
FY2026 consolidated operating margin was 20.3% (down from 21.1% in FY2025), with the Labour Codes impact of ₹1,289 crore reducing consolidated operating margin by 0.7 percentage points.
FY2026 free cash flow was ₹33,097 crore, representing 112.3% of net profit, and the company completed a ₹18,000 crore buyback at ₹1,800 per share.

comparisons.promise: January 2026 (Q3 FY26) call: revenue growth guidance revised upward to 3%–3.5% constant currency for FY2026; operating margin guidance maintained at 20%–22%.
comparisons.actual: FY2026 delivered 3.1% constant-currency revenue growth and 21.0% adjusted operating margin (20.3% reported, including 0.7pp Labour Codes impact).
comparisons.rationale: 3.1% CC growth falls within the 3%–3.5% guided range, and the 21.0% adjusted margin is within the 20%–22% band; the reported 20.3% margin is also within the band even before adjustment.

comparisons.promise: April 2026 (Q4 FY26) call: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 1.5%–3.5% YoY in constant currency; operating margin guidance of 20%–22%.
comparisons.actual: As of the October 2026 (Q2 FY27) call, guidance was revised down to 1%–2% CC revenue growth; margin guidance maintained at 20%–22%. H1 FY27 CC growth was 1.9%.
comparisons.rationale: FY2027 ends 2027-03-31 and is still in progress as of the latest available quarter (Q2 FY27, ended 2026-09-30); the original April guidance was revised in July and again in October, so final delivery cannot yet be assessed.

comparisons.promise: April 2026 call: management expected H1 FY27 to be stronger than H2, consistent with normal seasonality, and expected acceleration in Financial Services and EURS verticals.
comparisons.actual: Q1 FY27 CC revenue growth was 2.4% YoY, but management stated Q1 revenue growth was lower than expectations due to a one-off 50bps EURS client program termination, softer volumes, and softer pricing; operating margin was 21.1%.
comparisons.rationale: The margin held within guidance and growth was positive, but management explicitly characterized Q1 revenue growth as below their expectations, and the H1-stronger-than-H2 expectation was subsequently revised as guidance was cut in July.

comparisons.promise: July 2026 call: revised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1.5%–3% CC, including ~1.7% from acquisitions (Optimum Healthcare and Stratus); margin guidance maintained at 20%–22%.
comparisons.actual: Q2 FY27 CC revenue growth was 1.5% YoY (1.2% sequential), below management's expectations due to softer volumes and lower-than-anticipated price increases; operating margin was 21.0%; guidance was cut again to 1%–2% CC.
comparisons.rationale: Q2 margin of 21.0% remained within the 20%–22% band, but revenue growth came in below management's own expectations, prompting a second consecutive guidance cut; the full-year 1.5%–3% range remains technically open but H1 tracking (1.9%) is near the low end.

watch.text: Pricing pressure from competitive intensity: management noted that the pricing expansion expected at the start of FY27 has not materialized, with lower-than-anticipated price increases amid high competitive intensity, particularly around AI-led productivity commitments.
Discretionary spend softness in Retail and Hi-Tech: management called out slower discretionary spend in these sectors, with Retail impacted by ramp-downs and Hi-Tech by budget cuts at large clients.

Large deal conversion and mega deal ramp: the $2bn+ seven-year net-new mega deal signed in Q2 FY27 is expected to contribute over 1% growth in FY28, with transition beginning in H2 Q4 FY27; execution on this and the $8.8bn H1 large deal TCV will be key to FY28 growth.

limitations: The latest four reported quarters in the sources are Q3 FY26 (Jan 2026 call), Q4 FY26 (Apr 2026 call), Q1 FY27 (Jul 2026 call), and Q2 FY27 (Oct 2026 call); these are consecutive and used for comparisons.
FY2027 annual guidance (1%–2% CC revenue growth as of October 2026) is still in progress and cannot be finally assessed until the year ends on 2027-03-31.
The February 2026 transcript is an AI Investor Day, not a quarterly results call, so it contains no quarterly guidance to compare against delivery.

Quarterly revenue and margin figures cited from transcripts are in USD and constant-currency terms as stated by management; the annual report provides only annual Ind AS consolidated figures, so direct quarterly-to-annual reconciliation is not possible from these excerpts.
The annual report does not provide quarterly breakdowns of revenue or margin, limiting the ability to verify quarterly transcript figures against audited financials.

Trade receivables and contract balances
The timing of revenue recognition, billings and cash collections 
results in receivables, unbilled revenue, and unearned revenue 
on the Group’s Consolidated Balance Sheet. Amounts are billed 
as work progresses in accordance with agreed-upon contractual 
terms, either at periodic intervals (e.g., monthly or quarterly) or 
upon achievement of contractual milestones.
The Group’s receivables are rights to consideration that are 
unconditional. Unbilled revenues comprising revenues in excess 
of billings from time and material contracts and fixed-price 
maintenance contracts are classified as financial asset when 
the right to consideration is unconditional and is due only 
after a passage of time.
Invoicing to the clients for other fixed-price contracts is based on 
milestones as defined in the contract and therefore the timing of 
revenue recognition is different from the timing of invoicing to 
the customers. Therefore unbilled revenues for other fixed-price 
contracts (contract asset) are classified as non-financial asset 
because the right to consideration is dependent on completion 
of contractual milestones.
Invoicing in excess of earnings are classified as unearned revenue.
Trade receivables and unbilled revenues are presented net of 
impairment in the Consolidated Balance Sheet.

The Group holds derivative financial instruments such as foreign 
exchange forward and option contracts to mitigate the risk of 
changes in exchange rates on foreign currency exposures. The 
counterparty for such contracts is generally a bank.
(i) Financial assets or financial liabilities, carried at fair value 
through profit or loss.
This category includes derivative financial assets or liabilities 
which are not designated as hedges.
Although the Group believes that these derivatives constitute 
hedges from an economic perspective, they may not qualify 
for hedge accounting under Ind AS 109, Financial Instruments. 
Any derivative that is either not designated as hedge, or 
is so designated but is ineffective as per Ind AS 109, is 
categorized as a financial asset or financial liability, at fair value 
through profit or loss.
Derivatives not designated as hedges are recognized initially at 
fair value and attributable transaction costs are recognized in 
net profit in the Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss when 
incurred. Subsequent to initial recognition, these derivatives are 
measured at fair value through profit or loss and the resulting 
exchange gains or losses are included in other income. Assets / 
liabilities in this category are presented as current assets / current 
liabilities if they are either held for trading or are expected to be 
realized within 12 months after the Balance Sheet date.
(ii) Cash flow hedge
Primarily, the Group designates certain foreign exchange 
forward and options contracts as cash flow hedges to mitigate 
the risk of foreign exchange exposure on highly probable 
forecast cash transactions.
When a derivative is designated as a cash flow hedging 
instrument, the effective portion of changes in the fair value of 
the derivative is recognized in other comprehensive income and 
accumulated in the cash flow hedge reserve. Any ineffective 
portion of changes in the fair value of the derivative is recognized 
immediately in the net profit in the Consolidated Statement 
of Profit and Loss. If the hedging instrument no longer meets 
the criteria for hedge accounting, then hedge accounting is 
discontinued prospectively. If the hedging instrument expires 
or is sold, terminated or exercised, the cumulative gain or loss 
on the hedging instrument recognized in cash flow hedge 
reserve till the period the hedge was effective remains in cash

During fiscal 2026, the Company continued running Project Maximus, a comprehensive margin expansion program structured across five 
pillars – Value-based selling; Efficient pyramid; Lean, automation and gen AI; Improving key portfolios, and Optimization of indirect costs. 
Value-based selling is a focused strategy to identify opportunities to align pricing to the value clients received for the services. Efficient 
pyramid brings in efficiencies to reduce effort costs by improving utilization, reducing sub-contractors, improving role mix, location 
mix, etc. Lean, Automation and gen AI is a strategic initiative to combine productivity and process improvement using automation 
technologies, including generative AI, to enhance efficiency. Improving key portfolios is a targeted approach to improve margins on 
large client engagements and service lines. Savings from Project Maximus, through the optimization of indirect costs, helped us invest in 
strategic areas such as talent, AI, and sales and marketing.

Trade receivables and Contract Balances
The timing of revenue recognition, billings and cash collections 
results in receivables, unbilled revenue, and unearned revenue 
on the Company’s Balance Sheet. Amounts are billed as work 
progresses in accordance with agreed-upon contractual terms, 
either at periodic intervals (e.g., monthly or quarterly) or upon 
achievement of contractual milestones.
The Company’s receivables are rights to consideration that 
are unconditional. Unbilled revenues comprising revenues in 
excess of billings from time and material contracts and fixed-
price maintenance contracts are classified as financial asset 
when the right to consideration is unconditional and is due only 
after a passage of time.
Invoicing to the clients for other fixed-price contracts is based on 
milestones as defined in the contract and therefore the timing of 
revenue recognition is different from the timing of invoicing to 
the customers. Therefore unbilled revenues for other fixed-price 
contracts (contract asset) are classified as non-financial asset 
because the right to consideration is dependent on completion of 
contractual milestones.
Invoicing in excess of earnings are classified as unearned revenue.
Trade receivables and unbilled revenues are presented net of 
impairment in the Balance Sheet.
During the year ended March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025, the 
company recognized revenue of `5,276 crore and `4,404 crore 
arising from opening unearned revenue as of April 1, 2025 and

snapshot.text: TCS is an IT services, consulting and business solutions provider offering a consulting-led, cognitive-powered, integrated portfolio of IT, business and engineering services, with reportable segments spanning BFSI, Manufacturing, Consumer Business, Communication/Media/Technology, Life Sciences & Healthcare and Others.

In FY2026 TCS closed the year with total contract value of US$40.7 billion including 5 mega deals; clients generating over US$100 million in annual revenue rose by 2 to 66, and the US$50 million band increased by 9 to 139 clients.

The Board recommended a final dividend of ₹31 per share, taking the total FY2026 dividend to ₹110 per share, and FY2026 operating cash flows were 105.9% of profit after tax attributable to shareholders.

financials.text: FY2026 consolidated revenue from operations was ₹267,021 crore, up 4.6% reported year-on-year, but down 2.4% in constant currency, with currency movements contributing a positive 7.0% impact on reported revenue.

FY2026 EBIT (before other income) was ₹66,838 crore at a 25.0% margin (up 70 bps from 24.3% in FY2025, a four-year high), and profit after tax attributable to shareholders was ₹52,820 crore, up 8.8%, with EPS of ₹145.99 (adjusted for bonus).

FY2026 reported profit before exceptional items and tax was ₹70,013 crore; exceptional items of ₹4,526 crore comprised restructuring expenses of ₹1,388 crore, statutory impact of new Labour Codes of ₹2,128 crore (gratuity ₹1,816 crore plus long-term compensated absences ₹312 crore), and a ₹1,010 crore provision towards a legal claim.

Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹73,188 crore, growing 0.5% sequentially and 2.8% year-on-year in constant currency, with an operating margin of 24%, net margin of 19%, TCV of US$9.6 billion (excluding the Porsche and Best Buy deals), and annualized AI services revenue crossing US$3.1 billion.

comparisons.promise: On the Q1 FY26 call (July 2025), management said Q1 delays were largely factored into Q1 numbers and, if there were no further delays, Q2 FY26 should be at least better than Q1 (qualitative outlook).
comparisons.actual: No Q2 FY26 outcome is present in the supplied excerpts: the next transcript provided is the Q1 FY27 call (July 2026), so the September 2025 quarter result cannot be verified.
comparisons.rationale: The promise exists in the July 2025 (Q1 FY26) transcript, but no Q2 FY26 transcript or quarterly results document is included in the inventory, so the outcome cannot be checked.

comparisons.promise: On the Q3 FY26 call management indicated aspiration to move margins towards 26% on a longer-term basis and to keep FY27 margins within a tighter reach after exiting FY26 at a four-year-high 25% annual margin (aspiration, not a dated quarterly commitment).
comparisons.actual: Q4 FY26 operating margin was 25.3% (up 10 bps sequentially) and FY26 full-year operating margin was 25.0%, a 70 bps expansion and a four-year high; the 26% aspiration remains a long-term goal, not yet due.
comparisons.rationale: The 26% margin is explicitly framed as a longer-term aspiration rather than dated guidance, so it cannot be scored met/missed against a specific quarter; the FY26 exit margin of 25% is consistent with the stated four-year-high framing.

comparisons.promise: On the Q4 FY26 call (April 2026), management said the immediate FY27 headwind would be annual increments and that margins would be balanced within a tighter reach, with the usual levers and non-employee expense optimization (qualitative outlook).
comparisons.actual: Q1 FY27 operating margin was 24%, declining 130 bps sequentially, with annual increments impacting margins by 170 bps, partly offset by 40 bps currency benefit and operational efficiencies.
comparisons.rationale: The anticipated increment headwind materialized (170 bps impact) and margins declined as flagged, but the company also delivered partial offsets (currency, efficiencies), consistent with its 'balance' framing; no numeric margin target was set for Q1, so a met/missed verdict is not appropriate.

comparisons.promise: On the Q4 FY26 call, management said most known client-specific headwinds were behind and expressed positivity about FY27 international growth, while declining to put a number on the growth recovery (qualitative outlook).
comparisons.actual: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 2.2% sequentially and 13.9% year-on-year in rupee terms (0.4% QoQ and 3.2% YoY in constant currency), described as the fourth consecutive quarter of growth, with TCV of US$9.5 billion including an US$800 million SKF mega deal.
comparisons.rationale: The promise was explicitly non-numeric optimism about FY27; a single quarter of positive growth neither proves nor refutes a full-year qualitative outlook, so it is assessed as not comparable rather than met/missed.

comparisons.promise: On the Q1 FY27 call (July 2026), management said it wants to exit FY27 at 25%+ EBIT margin and strive to achieve it sooner rather than later (explicit timeline tied to fiscal-year exit).
comparisons.actual: Not yet due: the latest reported quarter in the sources is Q2 FY27 with operating margin of 24%, and the FY27 exit (Q4 FY27) outcome is not available as of the analysis date.
comparisons.rationale: The promise targets the FY27 exit margin; with only Q1 and Q2 FY27 reported (24% in both), the commitment cannot be judged until Q4 FY27 results are available.

watch.text: Margin trajectory vs. investment drag: Q2 FY27 gross margin declined sequentially on higher subcontractor and third-party costs, and management flagged ~50 bps of acquisition-related dilution from MHP plus furlough seasonality as H2 FY27 headwinds while reiterating the long-term 26–28% aspiration; watch whether margins 'inch up' as promised.

North America and India/regional recovery: management said North America revenue should 'recover and become healthy soon' and that deferred India regional-market revenue should return in the medium term without a specific date; watch Q3/Q4 FY27 for delivery on these qualitative commitments.

Data center (HyperVault) revenue timing: management stated data-center capacity creation follows contract wins and revenues will take about 18–24 months to start kicking in; watch for contract announcements and the resulting revenue timeline.

limitations: The latest four consecutive reported quarters represented in the sources are Q1 FY26 (Jun-2025 quarter, from the July 2025 call), Q4 FY26 (Mar-2026 quarter, April 2026 call), Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 quarter, July 2026 call) and Q2 FY27 (Sep-2026 quarter, October 2026 call); transcripts for Q2 FY26 (Oct 2025) and Q3 FY26 (Jan 2026) are not in the inventory, so quarter-over-quarter continuity across FY26 is broken and no outcome evidence exists for those quarters.

TCS explicitly states on each call that it does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance; most forward-looking statements are qualitative outlooks or aspirations and are assessed as not_comparable rather than met/missed.

The 26–28% margin band is described by management as a long-term aspiration/North Star, and the FY27 exit target of 25%+ is not yet due as of 2026-11-15; neither can be scored against current results.
Annual FY2026 guidance comparisons are not possible because no prior-year annual quantitative guidance document is included in the inventory; FY2026 outcomes are reported only as actuals.

AI services revenue (US$2.3bn → US$2.6bn → US$3.1bn annualized) is a management-disclosed metric without a published reconciliation in the supplied excerpts; its definition and comparability across quarters cannot be independently verified from these sources.
Q2 FY27 TCV of US$9.6 billion explicitly excludes the Porsche and Best Buy deals, so TCV comparisons across quarters may not be like-for-like.

12)	 Revenue recognition
	
The Group earns revenue primarily from providing IT services, consulting and business solutions. The Group offers a consulting-led, 
cognitive powered, integrated portfolio of IT, business and engineering services and solutions.
	
Revenue is recognised upon transfer of control of promised products or services to customers in an amount that reflects the 
consideration which the Group expects to receive in exchange for those products or services.
 
 
Revenue from time and material and job contracts is recognised on output basis measured by units delivered, efforts 
expended, number of transactions processed, etc.
 
 
Revenue related to fixed price maintenance and support services contracts where the Group is standing ready to provide 
services is recognised based on time elapsed mode and revenue is straight-lined over the period of performance.
 
 
In respect of other fixed-price contracts, revenue is recognised using percentage-of-completion method (‘POC method’) of 
accounting with contract costs incurred determining the degree of completion of the performance obligation. The contract 
costs used in computing the revenues include cost of fulfilling warranty obligations.
 
 
Revenue from the sale of distinct internally developed software and manufactured systems and third party software 
is recognised upfront at the point in time when the system / software is delivered to the customer. In cases where 
implementation and / or customisation services rendered significantly modifies or customises the software, these services and 
software are accounted for as a single performance obligation and revenue is recognised over time on a POC method.
 
 
Revenue from the sale of distinct third party hardware is recognised at the point in time when control is transferred 
to the customer.
 
 
The solutions offered by the Group may include supply of third-party equipment or software. In such cases, revenue for supply 
of such third party products are recorded at gross or net basis depending on whether the Group is acting as the principal or as 
an agent of the customer. The Group recognises revenue in the gross amount of consideration when it is acting as a principal 
and at net amount of consideration when it is acting as an agent.
	
Revenue is measured based on the transaction price, which is the consideration, adjusted for volume discounts, service level 
credits, performance bonuses, price concessions and incentives, if any, as specified in the contract with the customer. Revenue also 
excludes taxes collected from customers.

How the matter was addressed in our audit
The Company inter alia engages in Fixed-price contracts, wherein, 
revenue is recognised using percentage of completion computed 
as per the input method based on the Company’s estimate of 
contract costs.
We identified revenue recognition of fixed price contracts where 
the percentage of completion is used as a key audit matter since –
 
 
there is an inherent risk and presumed fraud risk around the 
accuracy and existence of revenues recognised considering 
the customised and complex nature of these contracts and 
significant inputs of IT systems;
 
 
application of revenue recognition using percentage of 
completion under accounting standard (Ind AS 115, Revenue 
from Contracts with customers) is complex and involves 
estimating the future cost-to-completion of these contracts, 
which is used to measure the stage of completion of the 
relevant performance obligations;
 
 
these contracts may involve onerous obligations which 
requires critical assessment of foreseeable losses to be made 
by the Company; and
 
 
at year-end, significant amount of contract assets, unearned 
and deferred revenue balances related to these contracts are 
recognised on the balance sheet.

Obtained an understanding of the systems, processes and 
controls implemented by the Company for recording and 
computing revenue and the associated contract assets, 
unearned and deferred revenue balances.
 
 
Involved our Information technology (‘IT’) specialists, as 
required and assessed the IT environment in which the 
business systems operate.

Operating segments are defined as components of an enterprise for which discrete financial information is available that is 
evaluated regularly by the chief operating decision maker, in deciding how to allocate resources and assessing performance. The 
Group’s chief operating decision maker is the Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director.
	
The Group has identified business segments (‘industry vertical’) as reportable segments. The business segments comprise:  
1) Banking, Financial Services and Insurance, 2) Manufacturing, 3) Consumer Business, 4) Communication, Media and Technology, 
5) Life Sciences and Healthcare and 6) Others such as Energy, Resources and Utilities, s-Governance and Products.
	
Revenue and expenses directly attributable to segments are reported under each reportable segment. Expenses which are 
not directly identifiable to each reporting segment have been allocated on the basis of associated revenue of the segment. 
All other expenses which are not attributable or allocable to segments or are non-recurring in nature have been disclosed as 
unallocable expenses.
	
The assets and liabilities of the Group are used interchangeably amongst segments. Allocation of such assets and liabilities is not 
practicable and any forced allocation would not result in any meaningful segregation. Hence assets and liabilities have not been 
identified to any of the reportable segments.

snapshot.text: Dixon Technologies (India) Limited is an electronics manufacturing services company whose consolidated revenue from operations for FY2025-26 (year ended March 31, 2026) was ₹48,87,280 lakhs (₹48,873 crores), up from ₹38,86,010 lakhs in FY2024-25; the Mobile Phones and Other EMS vertical contributed ₹4,42,570 million (~90%) of consolidated revenue.

The company operates through multiple verticals including Mobile Phones and Other EMS (₹4,42,570 million), Consumer Electronics & Refrigerator (₹28,920 million), and Home Appliances & Engineering (₹14,260 million) in FY2025-26; it also has a 51% camera-module subsidiary Q Tech and a 74:26 display-module JV with HKC.
The company closed FY2025-26 with a negative working capital cycle of 8 days, net debt of ₹(7,730) million, ROCE of 44.8% and ROE of 28.1%.

financials.text: Consolidated revenue from operations for FY2025-26 was ₹48,87,280 lakhs vs ₹38,86,010 lakhs in FY2024-25, growth of ~26% YoY (management cites ₹48,893 crores excluding exceptional gain).
Consolidated profit for the year FY2025-26 was ₹1,64,425 lakhs vs ₹1,23,258 lakhs in FY2024-25, with basic EPS of ₹271.59 vs ₹205.70 (nominal value ₹2).

Consolidated EBITDA excluding exceptional gain for FY2025-26 was ₹1,887 crores vs ₹1,528 crores in FY2024-25, a growth of 23% (management-stated adjusted figure; annual report shows EBITDA of ₹25,796 million including other income).
Consolidated adjusted PAT after minority interest (excluding exceptional gain) for FY2025-26 was ₹845 crores vs ₹706 crores in FY2024-25, a growth of 20% (management-stated adjusted figure).

comparisons.promise: In the Aug 2026 (July 31, 2026) call, management guided to 20-25% quarter-on-quarter mobile volume growth in Q2 vs Q1, with a Q2 order book of ~9-9.2 million units and H1 of ~16-16.5 million (excluding Vivo).

Consumer Electronics, that is LED TVs and refrigerators: 
Revenues for the quarter was INR 1,115 crores and operating profit of INR 40 crores. Our LED 
TV and refrigerator business are operating in a challenging environment characterized by overall 
softness in consumer demand and inflationary pressures across key input costs.  
 
However, we remain focused on expanding our customer base, increasing ODM participation, 
and strengthening our product portfolio. We believe the current demand is cyclical rather than 
structural and Dixon remains well positioned to benefit as industry volumes normalize. LED 
TVs demand in value and mid-range remains soft, impacted by sharp input cost inflation driven 
primarily by global memory supply tightness. However, demand for large-screen televisions, 
that is 50 inches and above, and premium QLED and OLED models remained relatively healthy.  
 
We have initiated local mini-LED production and plan to transition fully to an ODM model by 
Q3 of the current fiscal based on the customer demand and market feedback. We have also 
integrated low-cost mainboard support for lightweight operating systems, that is Coolita, AOSP, 
and Thundercloud, into our Q3 product portfolio.  
 
Refrigerators: 
Q2 also saw an uptick in commodity prices and elevated sea freight costs, which necessitated 
corresponding increase in selling prices, which further weighed on consumer demand and 
impacted near-term volume growth. Despite an industry-wide decline in direct cool segment, we 
sustained our volumes with portfolio enhancement and onboarding new brands. For a large brand 
now, we have started manufacturing side-by-side refrigerators and will start manufacturing 
multi-door French door refrigerators from next month.  
 
To support future growth, we are expanding our current facility by almost 375,000 square feet, 
creating capacities for deep freezers, visi coolers, and two-door refrigerators. This expansion 
will enhance our value mix and establish a broader, more robust appliance platform over time.  
 
Despite the near-term softness, we remain positive on medium to long-term growth prospects of 
category supported by low household penetration, premiumization, and increasing customer 
demand.

snapshot.text: Persistent Systems delivered USD 487.6 million revenue in Q2 FY27 (quarter ended Sep 30, 2026), up 7.8% QoQ and 20% YoY, marking its 26th consecutive sequential quarter of revenue growth.

The company is acquiring Nagarro: it secured approximately 94.04% of Nagarro share capital (excluding treasury shares) via a voluntary public takeover offer at €81 per share, exceeding the 50%+1 minimum acceptance threshold, with deal closure expected by Q4-CY26 or Q1-CY27.

Persistent's AI-led platforms (SASVA, iAURA, GenAI Hub) are embedded in client engagements; in Q3 FY26, tool-driven pricing models on engagements signed the prior quarter contributed 150 basis points of EBIT margin improvement.

financials.text: Q2 FY27 (quarter ended Sep 30, 2026): revenue USD 487.6 million (Rs. 46,639 million, +30.3% YoY); EBIT Rs. 6,977.2 million at 15.0% margin (down 130 bps YoY); reported PAT Rs. 3,515.1 million (7.5% margin, -25.4% YoY), including ~3.1% impact from Nagarro transaction costs of Rs. 1,853.4 million; operating PAT margin 10.6%.

FY26 (year ended Mar 31, 2026): consolidated revenue USD 1,654.4 million (Rs. 147,484.5 million, +23.5% YoY in INR); EBIT margin 15.6% (+90 bps YoY); PAT margin 12.6%; annual report shows consolidated PAT of Rs. 18,651.20 million for FY26 vs Rs. 14,001.61 million in FY25.

Q2 FY27 bookings: TCV USD 633.5 million and ACV USD 481 million (new bookings TCV USD 367.1 million, ACV USD 262.3 million); trailing-twelve-month TCV growth was 36.3% and ACV growth 21.9% per management.

Balance sheet and cash: total cash and investments stood at Rs. 29,996.7 million (~USD 315 million) as of Sep 30, 2026 vs Rs. 27,044 million at end of prior quarter; billed DSO improved to 50 days from 61 days; ROCE (ex-cash) 45.6% vs 43.6% prior quarter.

comparisons.promise: Management aspiration of 16-17% EBIT margin range (stated as aspiration, not guidance, in the Apr 2026 call: 'we have achieved whatever we had said... Our aspiration continues to be in the 16 to 17% range').
comparisons.actual: FY26 EBIT margin came in at 15.6% (+90 bps YoY); Q4 FY26 EBIT margin was 16.3%.
comparisons.rationale: Management explicitly frames the 16-17% range as an aspiration, not guidance, and notes growth/investment is the first priority; a full-year 15.6% margin cannot be scored against an explicitly non-binding aspiration. Q4 FY26 at 16.3% did touch the lower end of the range, but the aspiration is a continuing trajectory, not a dated promise.

comparisons.promise: Large deal (announced Q1 FY27, ~$650M TCV / $125M ACV) to be 'accretive - revenue & margin from Q2 onwards' with 'fairly healthy' margins (Aug 2026 call).
comparisons.actual: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 7.8% QoQ / 20% YoY to USD 487.6 million, with high-tech-led growth; however, the deal's third-party tools/licenses investment added ~USD 4 million quarterly amortization, a 90 bps drag on Q2 EBIT margin, and EBIT margin declined 100 bps QoQ to 15%.
comparisons.rationale: Revenue accretion clearly materialized (strong QoQ growth attributed partly to the large deal and a BFSI vendor-consolidation win). Margin accretion is not evidenced at company level: the deal contributed a 90 bps margin headwind via amortization in Q2, and management said margin impact will reduce only as spend is optimized and revenue scales. The 'fairly healthy margins' claim for the deal itself cannot be verified from disclosed segment data.

comparisons.promise: One-time Nagarro transaction expenses of approximately USD 50 million spread over three to four quarters, weighing on reported EPS (Oct 2026 call); Rs. 1,853.4 million (~USD 21 million) incurred in Q2 with USD 25-30 million incremental expected over next two to four quarters.
comparisons.actual: Q2 FY27 reported PAT margin 7.5% (-25.4% YoY) and reported EPS Rs. 22.4 (-26% YoY), each impacted ~3.1% by these transaction costs; operating PAT margin was 10.6% (+5% YoY).
comparisons.rationale: The disclosed Q2 expense (Rs. 1,853.4 million) and the ~3.1% reported PAT/EPS impact are consistent with the stated plan of ~USD 50 million spread over 3-4 quarters, with USD 25-30 million more to come. The promise was about incurring these expenses on that schedule, which is tracking as stated; full USD 50 million is not yet complete, so this is an in-progress confirmation rather than a final verdict.

comparisons.promise: Aspiration of USD 2 billion annual revenue by March 2027 (reiterated in Jan 2026 call: 'we remain firmly on track, advancing confidently towards our aspiration of $2 billion by March 2027').
comparisons.actual: Not yet due: only Q2 FY27 (USD 487.6M) and Q3 FY26 (USD 422.5M, prior-year quarter) are in the supplied excerpts; no full-year FY27 outcome exists yet.
comparisons.rationale: The $2 billion by March 2027 target is explicitly labeled an aspiration and the fiscal year ends 2027-03-31, which is after the latest reporting date (Oct 2026 call covering Q2 FY27); no full-year FY27 outcome exists in the sources. Note also the pending Nagarro consolidation complicates like-for-like comparison.

watch.text: Nagarro integration and financing: remaining regulatory approvals (Austria, Spain, RBI), squeeze-out of minorities, replacing the €1.4 billion 18-month bridge loan with long-term financing including USD 1.25 billion debt/equity raise (USD 450 million equity or equity-linked), and incremental transaction costs of USD 25-30 million over the next two to four quarters.

Margin trajectory: management aspiration of 16-17% EBIT margin vs Q2 FY27's 15% after wage-hike (180 bps) and large-deal amortization (~90 bps) headwinds; watch whether FinOps/AI-led optimization reduces the large-deal margin drag as revenue scales.

Bookings momentum and demand: Q2 FY27 TCV of USD 633.5 million was soft YoY (~4% per an analyst) with management citing deal slippage and slower decision-making; watch whether TTM TCV growth (36.3%) holds and whether the large-deal ramp and BFSI vendor consolidation convert to sustained revenue.

limitations: Quarter continuity: the four transcripts provided map to Q3 FY26 (Jan 2026 call), Q4 FY26 (Apr 2026 call), Q1 FY27 (Aug 2026 call, excerpts cover the Nagarro/large-deal announcements), and Q2 FY27 (Oct 2026 call); however, the Aug 2026 excerpts provided contain no Q1 FY27 standalone financial results, so a complete four-quarter outcome series cannot be constructed from the excerpts supplied.

No explicit forward revenue or margin guidance is given by management in any excerpt (repeatedly stated 'we don't give forward looking guidance'); margin targets (16-17%) and revenue milestones ($2B by Mar 2027, $5B by FY31) are labeled aspirations and are assessed as not_comparable or not_yet_due accordingly.
The promised large-deal margin profile ('fairly healthy margins', accretive from Q2) cannot be verified against disclosed deal-level profitability; only company-level margin walkouts are available.

Annual Report 2026 excerpts provide FY26 consolidated financials (revenue Rs. 147,484.49 million; PAT Rs. 18,651.20 million) but the supplied pages do not include quarterly breakdowns or EBITDA reconciliation, so EBITDA is not inferred from operating profit.
Q3 FY26 TTM revenue is stated as '$1.6 million' in the Jan 2026 transcript, which appears to be a transcription error (likely USD 1.6 billion); the figure is not used in any claim.

Currency/scope: quarterly USD revenue figures are company-reported; rupee figures and margins are consolidated INR; the pending Nagarro acquisition (94.04% accepted, closing expected Q4-CY26/Q1-CY27) means FY27 figures remain pre-consolidation of Nagarro.

The Group derives revenues primarily from IT services comprising of software development and related services 
and from the licensing of software products. 
	
	
Arrangements with customers for software related services are either on a time-and-material or a fixed-price 
basis.
	
	
Revenue on time-and-material contracts are recognised as and when the related services are performed. 
Revenue from fixed-price contracts, where the performance obligations are satisfied over time and where there 
is no uncertainty as to measurement or collectability of consideration, is recognised as per the percentage-
of-completion method. When there is uncertainty as to measurement or ultimate collectability, revenue 
recognition is postponed until such uncertainty is resolved. 
	
	
Revenue from licenses where the customer obtains a “right to use” the licenses is recognised at the time 
the license is made available to the customer. Revenue from licenses where the customer obtains a “right to 
access” is recognised over the access period.
	
	
When support services are provided in conjunction with the licensing arrangement and the license and the 
support services have been identified as two separate performance obligations, the transaction price for such 
contracts are allocated to each performance obligation of the contract based on their relative standalone 
selling prices. Maintenance revenue is recognised proportionately over the period in which the services are 
rendered.
	
	
Revenue from revenue share is recognised in accordance with the terms of the relevant agreements.
	
	
Unbilled revenue represents revenue recognised in relation to work done until the balance sheet date for which 
billing has not taken place.

Impairment of financial assets
	
	
	
The Company applies Expected Credit Loss (ECL) model for measurement and recognition of impairment 
loss on financial assets measured at amortised cost and financial assets that are debts instruments and are 
measured at FVTOCI. ECL is the difference between contractual cash flows that are due and the cash flows 
that the Company expects to receive, discounted at the original effective interest rate.
	
	
	
For trade receivables, the Company recognises impairment loss allowance based on lifetime ECL at each 
reporting date, right from its initial recognition. The Company recognises lifetime expected losses for all 
contract assets and / or all trade receivables that do not constitute a financing transaction. In determining the 
allowances for doubtful trade receivables, the Company has used a practical expedient by computing the 
expected credit loss allowance for trade receivables based on a provision matrix. The provision matrix takes 
into account historical credit loss experience and is adjusted for forward looking information. The expected 
credit loss allowance is based on the ageing of the receivables that are due and allowance rates used in the 
provision matrix. For all other financial assets, expected credit losses are measured at an amount equal to the 
12 months expected credit losses or at an amount equal to the lifetime expected credit losses if the credit risk 
on the financial asset has increased significantly since initial recognition.

Compensated absences and long service awards
	
	
Leave encashment
	
	
Accumulated leave, which is expected to be utilised within the next twelve months, is treated as short-term 
employee benefit. The Group measures the expected cost of such absences as the additional amount that it 
expects to pay as a result of the unused entitlement that has accumulated at the reporting date.
	
	
The Group treats accumulated leave expected to be carried forward beyond twelve months, as long-term employee 
benefit for measurement purposes. Such long-term compensated absences are provided for based on the actuarial 
valuation using the projected unit credit method at the reporting date. Remeasurements, comprising of actuarial gains 
and losses are recognised in full in the consolidated financial statement of profit and loss. Expense on non-accumulating 
compensated absences is recognised in the period in which the absences occur.
	
	
The expected cost of accumulating leave encashment is determined by actuarial valuation performed by an 
independent actuary at each balance sheet date using projected unit credit method on the additional amount 
expected to be paid / availed as a result of the unused entitlement that has accumulated at the balance sheet date. 
Expense on non-accumulating leave encashment is recognised in the period in which the absences occur. 
	
	
Long service awards
	
	
Long service awards are other long term benefits to all eligible employees, as per the Group’s policy. The cost of 
providing benefit under long service awards scheme is determined on the basis of actuarial valuation performed 
by independent actuary using the projected unit credit method at the reporting date. Remeasurements, 
comprising of actuarial gains and losses are recognised in full in the consolidated statement of profit and loss.
	
	
During the year, the group has discontinued the said policy.
	
	
Other employee benefits
	
	
Other short-term employee benefits such as overseas social security contributions and performance incentives 
expected to be paid in exchange for services rendered by employees, are recognised in the consolidated 
statement of profit and loss during the period when the employee renders the service.

compute the amount are those that are enacted or substantively enacted, at the reporting date. Current income 
tax relating to items recognised directly in equity is recognised in equity and not in the consolidated statement of

Note B -In previous years/periods, the Company had not accounted the depreciation impact on certain leasehold land (right of use assets), presented under Property Plant and Equipment in accordance with
Ind AS 116. The Company has now recognised the depreciation impact and adjusted the net carrying value of property, plant and equipment balance with corresponding impact to retained earnings as at 1
April 2025 and to ‘depreciation and amortisation expense’ line item of the respective periods presented in the standalone financial results.



Note C -During the year ended 31 March 2026, the Company had incorrectly accrued the interest income on loans given to subsidiaries. It has now been corrected and the Company has recognised additional
interest income in the respective periods presented in the standalone financial results with corresponding impact on interest accrued classified under other current financial assets.



Note D -In previous years/periods, the Company had inadvertently recognized revenue for certain sales transactions for which the transfer of control to customers was not completed as at the respective
reporting date. Accordingly, revenue, trade receivables, inventory, and cost of material consumed (COMC) have been reversed in the respective periods presented in the standalone financial results with
consequential impact on retained earnings as at 1 April 2025 and profit/loss of respective periods presented in the standalone financial results. Further, now such revenue and COMC have been recognised in
the correct periods with corresponding impact to trade receivable and inventory.


Note E -In previous years/periods, inventory balance was overstated due to excess overheads being inadvertently capitalized. Accordingly, the excess overheads recognized in inventory have now been
reversed, with a corresponding adjustments to retained earnings as at 1 April 2025 and COMC line item of the respective periods presented in the standalone financial results.



Note F -During the year ended 31 March 2026, the Company had not recognized provision against certain inventory items identified as slow-moving and non-moving items, which have now been recognised
appropriately with a charge to COGS line item of the respective periods presented in the standalone financial results with corresponding impact to inventory.


Note G -During the year ended 31 March 2026, the Company had not recognized adequate expected credit loss (ECL) provision against certain trade receivable which has now been recognised appropriately
with a charge to other expenses line item of the respective periods presented in the standalone financial results with corresponding impact to trade receivable.



Note H- In previous years/periods, the Company had inadvertently recognized erstwhile IPO and QIP related expenses under prepaid expenses with corresponding credit to other current liabilities which
has resulted in overstatement of prepaid expense and other current liabilities balance. Further, some of the prepaid expenses were in the nature of share issue expense, however, the same were not adjusted
with the securities premium account. It has now been corrected by crediting prepaid expenses with corresponding debit to other current liabilities and securities premium as at 1 April 2025 and 31 March
2026.



Note I - During the year ended 31 March 2026 and quarter ended 30 June 2026, the Company had erroneously classified purchase of traded goods under cost of material consumed, instead of presenting it
separately on the face of statement of profit and loss, which has now been corrected and the respective periods presented in the standalone financial results have accordingly been restated.


Note J- During the year ended 31 March 2026, the Company had made payment of GST demand to GST department pursuant to completion of GST audit, which was erroneously classified under Balance
with government authorities instead of charging it to statement of profit and loss account, which has now been corrected and the other expense amount presented under FY 26 column in the standalone
financial results has accordingly been restated.


Note K - The Company has erroneously written back the provision relating to employee incentives payables during the quarter ended 30 June 2026, which has now been reversed with adjustment to
employee incentive payables and corresponding impact on employee benefit expense line item presented in June 2026 quarter column in the standalone financial results.


Note L - In previous years/periods, the management had accounted for investment in equity shares of investee company inadvertently as financial assets at amortised cost, even though significant influence
being exercised by the Company over such investee company from the date of acquisition. Such investment should have been accounted for as an investment in associate at cost in accordance with Ind AS 28,
which has now been corrected.


Note M - The consequent tax impact of the aforesaid restatements has been recorded in retained earnings as at 1 April 2025 and tax expense of the respective periods presented in the standalone financial
results with corresponding adjustments to deferred tax and current tax assets/liability, as applicable.

Note B -
 In previous years/periods, the Group had recognised an intangible asset (manufacturing rights) and inadvertently presented the same under property plant and
equipment and also had not recognised any amortisation on such intangible asset. It has now been corrected by reclassifying it from PPE to Intangible Assets and the
Group has now recorded amortisation expense on it, which has impacted retained earnings as at 1 April 2025 and ‘depreciation and amortisation expense’ line item of
the respective periods presented in the consolidated financial results.

Note C -In previous years/periods, the management had erroneously computated foreign currency exchange differences and non-controlling interests (NCI) balance
pertaining to certain subsidiaries, which has now been corrected resulting in adjustment to these FSLI as at 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 with corresponding impact
on retained earnings as at 1 April 2025 and other comprehensive income of respective periods presented in the financial results.
Also, in the previous years, Goodwill pertaining to one subsidiary was overstated due to incorrect amount allocated to NCI balance, which has now been corrected by
adjusting goodwill with corresponding impact on NCI as at 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026.

Note D- In previous years/periods, the Group had recognized capital reserve arising from the acquisition of a subsidiary which was incorrectly adjusted against
goodwill arising from acquisition of certain other subsidiaries, which has resulted in understatement of capital reserve and goodwill. It has now been corrected and the
amounts of goodwill and the capital reserve as at 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 has been restated accordingly.

Note E-In previous years/periods, the management had accounted for investment in an investee company inadvertently as financial asset at amortised cost, even
though significant influence being exercised by the Group over such investee company from the date of acquisition. Such investment should have been accounted for as
an Investment in associate using the equity method of accounting in accordance with Ind AS 28. It has now been corrected retrospectively, and the equity pickup has
been done based on their interim/annual financial results/statements, with a quarter lag, as permitted under Ind AS 28. Further, subsequent funding during the year
ended 31 Mar 2026 in the investee company by external investors has resulted in dilution in Group’s stake with retained interest continues to be an associate,
accordingly, the Group has recorded dilution gain on deemed disposal of partial stake in accordance with Ind AS 28. As a result, the Group has corrected the
classification of investment in such associate from other non-current financial assets to a separate line item on the face of Balance Sheet and taken the impact to retained
earnings as at 1 April 2025, share of profit/loss from associate and other income in the respective periods presented in the consolidated financial results to correct the
accounting in accordance with Ind AS 28. Also, the same shall be required to be disclosed as Investment at cost.

evidence.text:
Note F:The Group has reclassified trade receivable expected to be realised beyond twelve months from the reporting date as at 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2026


Note G -In previous years/periods, with respect to a revenue contract, the Group had capitalized cost incurred under the head “Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE)”
and recognised depreciation on it and the monthly payments received as per the terms the agreement was recognized as rental income. In the current quarter,
management reassessed the accounting treatment and concluded that the contract falls within the scope of Service Concession Arrangements (SCA) under Appendix D
of Ind AS 115. As a result, the previously recorded PPE is derecognized and corresponding depreciation impact has now been reversed and accounting is corrected as
per revised assessment, which has impacted retained earnings as at 1 April 2025, PPE and receivable under SCA balance as at 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 and
finance income, revenue from operation, depreciation and cost of goods sold of respective periods presented in the consolidated financial results.

Note H :The consequent tax impact of the aforesaid restatements has been recorded in retained earnings as at 1 April 2025 and tax expense of the respective periods
presented in the consolidated financial results with corresponding adjustments to deferred tax and current tax assets/liability, as applicable


Note I:
In previous years/periods, inventory balance was overstated due to excess overheads being inadvertently capitalized. Accordingly, the excess overheads recognized in
inventory have now been reversed, with corresponding adjustments to retained earnings as at 1 April 2025 and COMC line item of the respective periods presented in
the consolidated financial results.
Note J:In previous years/periods, the Group had inadvertently recognized revenue for certain sale transactions for which the transfer of control to customers was not
completed as at the respective reporting date. Accordingly, revenue, trade receivables, inventory and cost of material consumed (COMC) have been reversed in the
respective periods presented in the consolidated financial results with consequential impact on retained earnings as at 1 April 2025 and profit/loss of respective periods
presented in the consolidated financial results. Further, now such revenue and COMC have been recognised in the correct periods with corresponding impact to trade
receivable and inventory.
Note K: During the year ended 31 March 2026, the Group had not recognized provision against certain inventory items identified as slow-moving and non-moving
items, which have now been recognised appropriately with a charge to COGS line item of the respective periods presented in the consolidated financial results with
corresponding impact to inventory.
Note: L During the year ended 31 March 2026, the Company had made payment of GST demand to GST department pursuant to completion of GST audit, which was
erroneously classified under Balance with government authorities instead of charging it to statement of profit and loss account, which has now been corrected and the
other expense amount presented under FY 26 column in the standalone financial results has accordingly been restated.
Note M:During the year ended 31 March 2026, the Group had erroneously recognised certain acquisition related cost under prepaid expenses which should have been
charged to Statement of profit and loss. It has now been corrected by reversal of such prepaid expense with corresponding impact to ‘other expenses’ line item in the
respective periods presented in the consolidated financial results.

Note N:In previous years/periods, the Group had inadvertently recognized erstwhile IPO and QIP related expenses under prepaid expenses with corresponding credit
to other current liabilities which has resulted in overstatement of prepaid expense and other current liabilities balance. Further, some of the prepaid expenses were in
the nature of share issue expense, however, the same were not adjusted with the securities premium account. It has now been corrected by crediting prepaid expenses
with corresponding debit to other current liabilities and securities premium as at 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026.


Note O:In previous years/periods, the Group had not accounted the depreciation impact on certain leasehold land (right of use assets), presented under Property Plant
and Equipment in accordance with Ind AS 116. The Group has now recognised the depreciation impact and adjusted the net carrying amount of property, plant and
equipment balance with corresponding impact to retained earnings as at 1 April 2025 and to ‘depreciation and amortisation expense’ line item of the respective periods
presented in the consolidated financial results.

Note P:In previous years/periods, the Group had acquired certain foreign subsidiaries and recognised customer contracts (identified intangible assets) and goodwill in
accordance with Ind AS 103. However, exchange differences arising on the translation of such goodwill and customer contracts were not recorded in the consolidated
financial results, in accordance with Ind AS 21, which has now been corrected by adjusting intangible assets and goodwill with corresponding impact to foreign
currency translation reserve as at 1 April 2025 and as at 31 March 2026 and the other comprehensive income of respective periods presented in the consolidated
financial results.
Note Q: The Group assessed that for one of the business acquisitions made during the year ended 31 March 2026, on account of incorrect working capital settlement
adjustment applied to purchase consideration, excess deferred consideration payable was recorded which has consequently resulted in overstatement of goodwill.
Accordingly, the same has now been corrected to reflect the correct contractual obligation of deferred consideration with a corresponding adjustment to Goodwill
initially recognised.

Note R:During the year ended 31 March 2026, the Group had not eliminated the interest income with the finance cost with respect to loans given by Holding Company
to subsidiaries, which has now been corrected by eliminating it with consequential impact on other income and finance cost line items in the respective periods
presented in the consolidated financial results.
Note S:During the year ended 31 March 2026 and quarter ended 30 June 2026, the Group had erroneously classified purchase of traded goods in cost of raw material
consumed, instead of presenting it separately on the face of statement of profit and loss, which has now been corrected and the respective periods presented in the
financial results have accordingly been restated.
Note T:
The Company has erroneously written back the provision relating to employee incentives payables during the quarter ended 30 June 2026, which has now been
reversed with adjustment to employee incentive payables and corresponding impact on employee benefit expense line item presented in June 2026 quarter column in
the standalone financial results.
Note U:During the year ended 31 March 2026, the Group had not recognised the ‘Right of use’ Asset for property taken on lease by one of the subsidiary and recorded
the lease rental expenses directly to statement of profit and loss account, which has now been corrected by recognizing Right of use asset and corresponding lease
liability along with subsequent measurement impact on these in accordance with the requirement of Ind AS 116 and reversed the accounting treatment given earlier. As
a result, adjustments are made to PPE (ROU) and lease liability with corresponding impact on ‘depreciation and amortisation expense’, ‘finance cost’ and ‘other
expense’ line items in the respective periods presented in the consolidated financial results.
